app/components/Section.js:1-14 — components take narrow props and know nothing about data fetching

app/components/TypeBadge.js:7 and app/app/pokemon/[name]/MovesTable.js:76 — the `type-${name}` class convention is stringly coupled to globals.css:142-159
coupling.rationale: Loose coupling with clear seams overall (api.js as the single data layer, prop-driven components, clean server/client split); the notable tangle is the undocumented row-shape contract between the Pokémon page and MovesTable.

evidence: app/lib/api.js:59-67 — `resource()` factory means adding an Items resource is one line; `mapToSpecies`, `getPokemonTypesMap` (api.js:100-121) and the `cached()` wrapper (api.js:36-56) are genuinely reusable

app/app/page.js:118-131 vs app/app/moves/[name]/page.js:52-58 vs app/app/abilities/[name]/page.js:36-42 vs app/app/types/[name]/page.js:54-61 — the species→PokemonCard mapping is copy-pasted four times with per-page prop tweaks instead of one CardList component
app/app/moves/[name]/page.js:25-52 vs app/app/pokemon/[name]/page.js:166-180 — the facts `<dl>` markup is duplicated between detail pages (only the CSS class is shared)
app/lib/api.js:96-104 and 108-110 — getSpeciesIndex and getTypeRecords are bespoke per-resource list loaders, so an /items index page starts from scratch
app/components/PokemonCard.js:13 — `hidden` is a single-page-specific boolean prop on a shared component, the start of flag-parameter creep
abstraction_design.rationale: The data-layer abstractions stretch well, but the view layer has none for the app's most repeated pattern (a list of Pokémon cards), and detail pages share markup only by duplication — a similar-but-different Items section means copying a page.

findings.issue: The species→PokemonCard mapping is duplicated at four list sites (home, move, ability, type) with per-page prop variations, so any change to card data or ordering is repeated.
findings.suggestion: Extract a `CardList({ species, ...cardProps })` component (or a `useCardList`-shaped helper around mapToSpecies) that owns the mapping, ordering and optional props; pages pass data plus options.

findings.issue: The row object shape produced by buildMovesSection in page.js is an implicit contract consumed by MovesTable via string keys (moveHref, typeKey, power, ...); renaming a key silently breaks the table.
findings.suggestion: Co-locate the row builder in MovesTable (or export a documented row factory from it) so the shape has one owner, or type/annotate the contract.

findings.issue: The type-label fallback `typeLabels.get(n) ?? humanize(n)` is re-implemented at five call sites (app/page.js:81,104; pokemon page:137; moves page:39; types page:32).
findings.suggestion: Add a `typeLabel(labels, name)` helper (or have getTypeLabels return objects with a labelOf method) so the fallback lives once.

findings.issue: `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` is repeated in all six route files; a change to the rendering/caching strategy is six edits and easy to miss one.
findings.suggestion: Declare it once in the root layout (segment config on layouts applies to child segments), or document the convention in a shared place; a future migration to cacheComponents would also be a single-site change.

findings.issue: The Next.js build output directory is committed and not gitignored (root .gitignore only covers /data/, /.data-cache/, node_modules/), so stale artifacts pollute diffs and source greps.
findings.suggestion: Add `.next/` to .gitignore and remove the committed artifacts.

findings.issue: The `hidden` prop and its `.hidden-note` CSS exist solely for the ability page, coupling a shared component to one feature and leaving dead code if Abilities is removed.
findings.suggestion: Let callers pass children/extra content, or move the hidden-ability note into an `extra` render slot owned by the ability page.

summary: A cleanly layered App Router app: one data module, thin prop-driven components, explicit client boundaries and a page-per-route structure that makes features easy to find and mostly easy to delete. The recurring weakness is page-level copy-paste — four hand-rolled card lists and duplicated detail-page markup — which turns card-wide changes into several edits. Framework usage is current and idiomatic for Next 16.4 LTS.

scenarios.change: Remove the Abilities pages and every link to them
scenarios.notes: Core removal is delete the route dir plus delete the Abilities Section (page.js:216-226) and its `abilities` const (:153); nav needs no edit. Optional but recommended cleanup: unused getAbility (api.js:69), the ability-only `hidden` prop (PokemonCard.js:27) and two dead CSS rules (globals.css:239,370).

scenarios.change: Fix wrong sprite for species whose default Pokémon has a different id/name
scenarios.notes: The sprite URL is built in one place (PokemonCard.js:17-22) and every list renders PokemonCard, so one fix covers all four lists — but the correct id must come from data: mapToSpecies (api.js:143) already derives the Pokémon's own id from its URL, while the home list uses species ids from getSpeciesIndex (api.js:96-104, passed at page.js:125). A complete fix needs a species→default-pokémon-id map in lib/api.js plus threading it through the home page.

scenarios.notes: mapToSpecies (api.js:146) is the single sort site for move/ability/type lists — one edit covers three pages — but the home list sorts separately (page.js) and, if sorting is a user control, needs URL state plus a client component; the other three pages have no controls at all and would need a new shared one. A CardList component would collapse most of this.

scenarios.change: Change the API base URL and caching rules
scenarios.notes: Excellent for the data side: base URL (api.js:3-4), the fetch/concurrency limiter (api.js:24-33) and the runtime cache (api.js:36-56) all live in one module and every fetch goes through fetchJson — one edit covers everything. The only scatter is `force-dynamic` repeated in six route files, which a root-layout segment config would collapse to one.
